history.summary: Hilltop Hanuman temple at 7,200 ft (~2,195 m), ~11 km from Gangtok on the Gangtok-Nathula highway, maintained by the Indian Army since 1968. Legend: Lord Hanuman rested here while carrying the Sanjeevani herb from the Himalayas to Lanka to save Lakshmana. A stone was worshipped in the open for a long time until Appaji Pant, an officer, built a Hanuman statue in the 1950s after a divine dream; the area was handed to the Indian Army in 1968 and has been maintained by it (17 Mountain Division) ever since. The round temple has a yellow-and-red hall with Ramayana murals, a room of subsidiary deities, a circular viewpoint with wooden ceiling, and prayer bells along the paved stairway. The royal cremation grounds (Lukshyama) of the Namgyal dynasty lie near the stairway entrance. FLAG: inHeritage.foundation's Hanuman Tok page claims an 1840 CE / late-19th-century origin and Indian Army construction - internally inconsistent and contradicted by all other sources; treated as unreliable. Coordinates from map geocode (FULL_ADDRESS match 'Hanuman Talk, 3rd Mile, Gangtok'), agreeing to ~10 m with inHeritage's published point (27.347835, 88.628696).

name: Hanuman Tok
town_description: Hanuman Tok crowns a ridge ~11 km above Gangtok on the Gangtok-Nathula highway, at 7,200 ft in Gangtok district. It commands a 360-degree panorama of valleys and the Kanchenjunga massif, and is a fixture of Gangtok sightseeing tours, commonly paired with Ganesh Tok and Tashi View Point. Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, blends Himalayan scenery with Hindu-Buddhist religious life.

travel.road: About 11 km from Gangtok city centre on the Gangtok-Nathula highway; taxi from any Gangtok hotel; easy paved stair climb from the parking lot with benches (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear skies (10-20 degC); early morning (6-9 AM) for peaceful darshan and sunrise over Kanchenjunga; Hanuman Jayanti (Mar-Apr) for celebrations (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 6:00 AM-7:00 PM daily, free entry (per inHeritage - verify). Dress modestly, remove footwear before the sanctum; photography inside the sanctum may be restricted.
